message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
### **ECG Interpretation**

#### **1. Technical Parameters**
* **Calibration:** Standard ($25\text{ mm/s}$, $10\text{ mm/mV}$, $1\text{ mV}$ calibration pulse shown at the left margin).

---

#### **2. Rate, Rhythm & Intervals**
* **Rhythm:** Normal Sinus Rhythm (upright P waves in lead II, regular P-QRS-T relationship).
* **Heart Rate:** $\approx 65\text{ bpm}$ (R-R interval $\approx 4.5 \text{ to } 5\text{ large boxes}$).
* **PR Interval:** Normal ($\approx 160\text{ ms} / 4\text{ small boxes}$).
* **QRS Duration:** Normal / narrow ($\approx 80\text{–}90\text{ ms}$).
* **Axis:** Leftward axis ($\approx 0^\circ \text{ to } -20^\circ$, positive in lead I, predominantly negative in III/aVF).

---

#### **3. Key Waveform & ST-T Findings**

* **Marked ST-Segment Elevation (Convex / "Tombstone" Morphology):**
  * **V1–V4:** Dramatic coved ST elevation (up to $6\text{–}7\text{ mm}$ in **V2–V3**, $\approx 3\text{–}4\text{ mm}$ in **V1**, $\approx 5\text{ mm}$ in **V4**).
  * **V5–V6:** Mild-to-moderate ST elevation ($\approx 1\text{–}2\text{ mm}$).
  * **High Lateral Leads (I, aVL):** ST elevation ($\approx 1.5\text{–}2\text{ mm}$ in **aVL**, $\approx 1\text{ mm}$ in lead **I**).
  * Loss of anterior R-wave progression with QS/rS complexes across V1–V3.

* **Reciprocal ST-Segment Depression:**
  * **Inferior Leads (III, aVF):** Significant reciprocal ST depression ($\approx 2\text{ mm}$ in **lead III** with T-wave inversion; $\approx 1\text{–}1.5\text{ mm}$ in **aVF**).

---

#### **4. Diagnostic Conclusion**
* **Acute Extensive Anterior ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)** (anteroseptal with lateral extension).
* **Likely Culprit Vessel:** Acute occlusion of the **proximal Left Anterior Descending (LAD) coronary artery** (evidenced by extensive ST elevation from V1 through V4/V5, ST elevation in aVL, and reciprocal ST depression in lead III).

> [!CAUTION]
> **Clinical Significance:** This is a critical medical emergency indicative of acute, transmural anterior myocardial infarction requiring immediate cardiac catheterization lab activation for emergent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
